text:
maya: quick RFC follow-up idea — combine lightweight client hint headers with a server-side pacing layer to smooth bursts without hard rejects.

alex: sketch it out please. curious how it differs from the existing quota admission stuff.

maya: two pieces: 1) clients optionally send X-client-hint: {preferred_qps, urgency} so we can optimistically allocate short-lived soft credits. 2) server maintains a per-tenant pacing token bucket + short predictive buffer that borrows from predicted near-future headroom (based on recent seq length and model).

ken: so soft credits are ephemeral, not billed? how do we avoid misuse?

maya: soft credits are meter-neutral for a tiny window (e.g., 500ms-5s). they let latency-sensitive tails get through. abuse def: require auth + entropy in header, track hint hit-rate and fall back to strict quota if suspicious.

alex: what about fairness across tenants? this sounds like it could favor big customers who can tweak hints.

maya: fairness enforced at pacing layer: global fairness lanes (latency-priority, cost-priority, default). hints can push you into a lane but only within limits based on historical spend and SLO weight. we still throttle envelopes when global pressure rises.

sri: curious about rollout safety. does this require client updates?

maya: optional client opt-in. default behavior unchanged. server will honor hints only for clients on an allowlist or when backend observes stable behavior. rollout plan: 1) telemetry-only (honor=false, surface metrics) 2) opt-in alpha for internal apps 3) public opt-in 4) safe default on with conservative limits.

julie: telemetry we should track: hit ratio (hint accepted/received), hint-lift (latency delta), abuse signals (hint spikes, repeated hint rejects), per-model cost delta.

maya: +1 on metrics. also add a per-tenant counter for "hint debt" so we can decay aggressive usage and revert to baseline if debt high.

ken: implementation sketch?

maya: server changes: small pacing service between ingress and admission. psuedocode: 
```
on_request(req):
  hint = parse(req.headers['X-Client-Hint'])
  lane = select_lane(req.tenant, hint)
  if pacing.allow(lane, hint.preferred_qps):
    mark_hint_accepted(req)
    pass_through()
  else:
    if fallback_policy == 'queue': queue_short(req, max_ms=200)
    else: respond_rate_limit()
```

alex: queueing with 200ms cap is good — avoids long tail. what about seq-length variance? long sequences can drain buffer.

maya: pacing uses predicted token-cost per-request (simple moving avg per endpoint/model), so the bucket is token-weighted not request-count. prediction is conservative by default.

ops-bot: note — added a telemetry dashboard stub: /dashboards/pacing-hints (created by ops-bot).

julie: threat model: crafted clients could set high urgency + low token estimates to game system. mitigation: sign hints server-side for trusted clients, validate token estimate against observed, escalate to strict quota on mismatch.

ken: how do we handle dedicated/private deployments where control plane differs?

maya: design is pluggable: core pacing logic lives in runtime and can be enabled/disabled via config. Private installs can supply different heuristics and trust models.

alex: perf overhead? extra hop could add ~1-2ms, ok given benefit. need microbenchmarks.

maya: action items: 1) draft mini-RFC with metrics + failure modes (maya) 2) prototype pacing shim in staging (ken + alex) 3) telemetry dashboard fleshed out (julie) 4) internal opt-in clients list (sri). aiming for telemetry-only by next sprint.

sri: +1, will coordinate internal opt-ins.

julie: adding unit tests for hint parsing and signed-hint verification.

maya: thanks all — leaving this thread as the follow-up tracker. ping me if you want to be on the prototype. :rocket:
